name: org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin
description: MCP Server Maven Plugin is a Maven plugin artifact with packaging type maven-plugin. It launches the Machai MCP Server directly from Maven builds and exposes Machai AI tools through the Model Context Protocol over HTTP. The plugin is intended for local development, testing, demonstrations, and integration workflows where users need to start an MCP server without a separate launcher. It provides Maven goals implemented by org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.HttpStatelessServerMojo and org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.HttpStreamableMcpServerMojo. The stateless goal starts a stateless HTTP MCP server, while the streamable goal starts a streamable HTTP MCP server. Shared configuration is implemented in org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.AbstractMCPServerMojo, which applies environment parameters, resolves Maven settings.xml server credentials, and passes custom configuration properties to the server. The plugin integrates with Maven project metadata, Maven settings credentials, Java 17, org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server, Apache Maven plugin APIs, and SLF4J logging. It is useful for AI-assisted development tools, MCP server lifecycle management, build-time server startup, HTTP MCP integration testing, and exposing Machai FunctionTools such as org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.tools.MCPServerTools.stopMcpServer(int).

usageContext: Start a Machai MCP server from a Maven project
Expose AI FunctionTools over Model Context Protocol HTTP endpoints
Run local MCP server instances for development or demonstrations
Configure server properties through Maven plugin parameters
Resolve credentials from Maven settings.xml using a server id
Control the MCP server lifecycle through plugin-provided tools

constructors.description: Creates a Maven Mojo instance that starts a stateless HTTP MCP server when Maven executes the corresponding plugin goal. Maven normally constructs this class through its plugin container rather than direct application code.

examples.description: Install and configure the plugin in a Maven pom.xml. Maven creates org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.HttpStatelessServerMojo internally when the stateless server goal is invoked. The configuration sets the HTTP port and passes runtime parameters to the Machai MCP server.

constructors.description: Creates a Maven Mojo instance that starts a streamable HTTP MCP server when Maven executes the corresponding plugin goal. Maven constructs this Mojo from plugin metadata during goal execution.

examples.description: Configure the plugin for a streamable MCP server scenario. The serverId value lets org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.AbstractMCPServerMojo resolve credentials and custom configuration from Apache Maven settings.xml before server startup.

constructors.description: Creates a utility object that implements org.machanism.machai.ai.tools.FunctionTools and exposes MCP server lifecycle operations, including delayed server shutdown.

examples.description: Direct Java usage scenario for tests or embedded tooling. The fully qualified org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.tools.MCPServerTools class is instantiated and its stopMcpServer method is called with exit code 0 to request a graceful delayed shutdown.

features.name: Start stateless HTTP MCP server
features.description: Executes the Maven Mojo that applies configured parameters, initializes an org.machanism.machai MCP stateless HTTP server with project name and version, sets the project directory and port, and starts the server. A org.apache.maven.plugin.MojoExecutionException is thrown if startup or configuration fails.

examples.description: Run a real Maven command to start a stateless HTTP MCP server for the current project. Use this after adding the plugin to pom.xml or when invoking the plugin with explicit Maven coordinates. The server listens on the configured port and exposes Machai AI tools through Model Context Protocol over HTTP.

features.name: Start streamable HTTP MCP server
features.description: Executes the Maven Mojo that applies configured parameters, initializes an org.machanism.machai MCP streamable HTTP server with project information, sets the project directory and port, and starts the server. This is suitable when clients need streamable MCP HTTP communication.

examples.description: Run a streamable MCP server from a Maven build. Configure the plugin in pom.xml first, optionally including params and serverId, then invoke the streamable server goal to expose MCP-compatible endpoints for clients that require streaming behavior.

features.name: Apply Maven parameters and credentials
features.description: Applies environment parameters and credentials to Java system properties. Each configured parameter is set as a system property if it is not already set. If a Maven server id is specified, the Mojo resolves credentials from Maven settings.xml and makes username, password, and custom configuration values available to downstream workflow execution.

examples.description: Configure Apache Maven settings.xml so org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.AbstractMCPServerMojo can resolve credentials for the configured serverId. This supports secure MCP server startup without hard-coding credentials in pom.xml.

features.name: Stop MCP server
features.description: Stops the MCP server by initiating a delayed shutdown, logging the shutdown event, waiting for a predefined delay, and then exiting the JVM with the supplied exit code. The method returns a message indicating that shutdown was initiated.

examples.description: Use the server lifecycle utility from Java code or a test harness. The example uses fully qualified Java types and calls stopMcpServer with exit code 0 to request graceful MCP server shutdown.

customizations.name: port
customizations.description: Maven plugin configuration property that selects the HTTP port used by the MCP server. The effective POM demonstrates port 45000 in plugin configuration.

examples.description: Set the MCP server HTTP port in the plugin configuration.

customizations.name: params
customizations.description: Map-like Maven plugin configuration used to pass runtime parameters such as gw.acts, gw.model, and embedding.model into Java system properties for the MCP server.

examples.description: Pass model, acts, and embedding configuration to the server through Maven plugin params.

customizations.name: serverId
customizations.description: Maven plugin configuration property used to identify a server entry in Apache Maven settings.xml. The plugin reads credentials and custom XML configuration from that server entry.

examples.description: Reference a Maven settings.xml server entry so credentials are not stored directly in project source files.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.AbstractMCPServerMojo
studs.description: Abstract base Mojo that defines the shared boundary for concrete MCP server Maven goals. It provides common configuration and credential resolution behavior for stateless and streamable server implementations.

examples.description: Illustrates the abstract Mojo extension pattern with fully qualified types. Concrete Mojos call applyParameters before starting their server implementation.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.ai.tools.FunctionTools
studs.description: Function tool contract implemented by org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.tools.MCPServerTools to expose callable server lifecycle operations to the Machai MCP tool layer.

examples.description: Treat MCPServerTools as the org.machanism.machai.ai.tools.FunctionTools contract when registering lifecycle functions with the tool layer.

examples.title: Install and configure the Maven plugin in pom.xml
steps: Add org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.2.2-SNAPSHOT to the build plugins section of pom.xml.
Configure the HTTP port used by the MCP server.
Provide params for Machai acts, generation model, and embedding model if required by your workflow.
Optionally configure serverId and add matching credentials to Apache Maven settings.xml.
examples.description: This example installs the ready-to-use Maven plugin component and configures it for real MCP server execution. The plugin can then be invoked from the command line to start HTTP MCP server variants.

examples.title: Configure credentials in Apache Maven settings.xml
steps: Open the user-level Maven settings.xml file, usually located at ~/.m2/settings.xml.
Add a server entry whose id matches the plugin serverId configuration.
Store username, password, and optional custom configuration values in that server entry.
Run the Maven plugin goal; org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.AbstractMCPServerMojo reads the server entry before startup.
examples.description: This configuration avoids storing credentials directly in pom.xml and lets the plugin resolve them through Maven settings at runtime.

examples.title: Run a stateless MCP server from the command line
steps: Ensure Java 17 and Apache Maven are installed.
Configure the plugin in pom.xml or invoke it with full Maven coordinates.
Run the stateless server goal with a port suitable for local development.
Connect an MCP-compatible HTTP client to the server endpoint exposed by the plugin.
examples.description: Starts the stateless HTTP MCP server for the current Maven project. This is useful for local AI tool integration testing and demonstrations.

examples.title: Run a streamable MCP server from the command line
steps: Ensure the plugin is available from a configured Maven repository, such as Maven Central snapshots for snapshot versions.
Configure plugin params and serverId in pom.xml if the server needs model or credential configuration.
Invoke the streamable server goal from the project root.
Use an MCP client that supports streamable HTTP behavior to communicate with the server.
examples.description: Starts a streamable HTTP MCP server variant. Use this when a client or workflow benefits from streaming server responses.
